segments.text: Good evening. This is Aakashwani. I am Shagun Chopra with the news at 9.
The headlines
Free trade agreement with New Zealand to come into force on the occasion of Vijay Dasmi
tomorrow. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Koyal says FTA will open new opportunities
for countries' exporters. Government asks Metta not to expose users to disproportionate
or one-sided narratives on its platforms. Action to be taken against online platforms
for unauthorized sale of regulated explosive substances. New Delhi rejects anti-India references
in organization of Islamic cooperation resolutions accuses Pakistan of misusing the organization.
Houthi attack on Yemen army camp in Shabwa kills 53 soldiers and in Asian para games India
bags 11 medals including four gold and five silver to take it standing to fourth position on day one.
And now the news in detail. India and New Zealand free trade agreement FTA will come
into force on the occasion of Vijadasmi tomorrow. The agreement will provide duty-free access
for 100% of Indian exports to New Zealand. Addressing the ceremony marking the entry
into force of the India-New Zealand free trade agreement in New Delhi today, Commerce
and Industry Minister Piyush Koyal said, the agreement opens significant new opportunities
industries for India's exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers and farmers.
We have agreed towards the goal of doubling bilateral two-way trade in goods and services
to New Zealand $7 billion or approximately 35,000 crores by 2030.
This will also facilitate $20 billion of investments into India, creating opportunities
industries, across manufacturing, infrastructure, agriculture, innovation and creating huge amount
of jobs and increasing our farmers' income."
Mr. Goyal expressed confidence that this win-win partnership will achieve many more milestones
guided by the shared vision of growth and mutual prosperity between the two nations.
A report
India has steadily expanded its global trade partnerships to strengthen economic growth,
create jobs and enhance its global standing. In recent years, the country has signed nine
free trade agreements covering 38 developed countries. The India-New Zealand FTA marks
a significant milestone in this effort. The FTA between the two countries was signed in April
this year at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The agreement protects India's farmers' interests,
boosts labour-intensive sectors like textiles and leather and opens new opportunities for
Indian professionals, students and service providers. The bilateral, merchandise trade between
in India and New Zealand stood at around US$1.1 billion in 2025-2026. For the first time,
New Zealand has facilitated trade in Ayurveda, yoga and other traditional medicine services
with India, with Dipendra Anand Kumar for Akarsmani News, Delhi.
On the occasion, the first ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was
flagged off by the Commerce Minister today. Tomorrow, on the entry into forced-day flag-offs
are planned for a range of products across agriculture, gems and jewelry, engineering
and others.
The US Secretary of State Marco Rubio today said that the United States is close to finalizing
a trade deal with India. He was speaking to reporters in Samarkand, Uzbekistan today.
Mr. Rubio defended Washington's decision to temporarily waive off sanctions for countries
importing Russian oil and gas, saying the move was aimed at easing pressure on global
energy supplies and prices.
We're trying to finalize a trade deal with India right now.
We're very close to doing that.
Every country has a complex set of factors that they have to take into account.
Geography is real.
For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources.
That's not an excuse, but all that has to be balanced when you make foreign policy.
The foreign policy of the United States, of course, takes into account what's happening
with the war between Russia and Ukraine, but it is not solely dominated by that.
It has to take into account a variety of other factors, including our bilateral
relationships with other countries.
Mr. Rubio is scheduled to visit Mumbai tomorrow, where he will meet external affairs minister
Dr. S. Jai Shankar. Later, he is expected to travel to Jhamnagar.
Government has asked Metta, the owner of Instagram and Facebook, to ensure that its
recommendations systems do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single
or limited set of narrative. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
suggested in an advisory that the company step up checks on content that could cause
public disorder or incite violence or other unlawful activity.
It further asked Metta to undertake appropriate measures to provide adequate context in relation
to photographs, videos, graphics or other content depicting ongoing public events.
India has categorically rejected the anti-India references in the resolutions of the Organisation
of Islamic Cooperation, OIC, Council of Foreign Ministers' Meeting, held in Baghdad between
the 17th and 18th of this month. The Ministry of External Affairs in a statement said,
references to India are malicious, biased and false, and have been orchestrated by Pakistan.
It accused Pakistan of orchestrating the references and misusing the OIC to pursue its agenda.
The ministry reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are integral parts of India
and that the Organization of Islamic Cooperation has no right to comment on India's internal
matters.
The MEA said, since the abrogation of Article 370, Jammu and Kashmir has witnessed significant
economic growth, infrastructure development, and a boost in tourism and connectivity.
It also accused Pakistan of using violence and repression against civilian protesters
in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, resulting in the deaths of scores of people
including women and children.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Stay connected with AIR News, Follow us on X at AIR News Alerts and visit newsonair.gov.in
for the latest updates.
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivrat Singh Chauhan today launched the upgraded
Agri Welfare Portal for Farmers.
The portal aims to provide farmers across the country with direct, easy access to
government schemes, financial assistance and reliable agricultural information on their
mobile phones.
I am confident that this portal will prove to be revolutionary in providing farmers with
the right information at the right time.
This is truly an important step towards advancing the vision of digital India, good governance
and farmers welfare, envisioned by the Prime Minister, Narendra Modi.
Indian railways has issued an advisory cautioning passengers against playing music, videos or
other audio on mobile phones in speaker mode on trains and railway premises. Any passenger
found causing a nuisance by doing so can be removed from railway premises and will
be fined up to Rs 1,000. Railway authorities can also seize the passenger's ticket
or pass depending on the circumstances. The Election Commission has shared frequently
asked questions or FAQs on electoral process, saying that special intensive revision, SIR,
seeks to ensure that no eligible Indian citizen is excluded from the electoral role. It added
that the aim of the exercise is to identify and remove any invalid entries like those
relating to deceased persons, duplicate registrations, permanently shifted electors, foreigners
and persons otherwise ineligible for electoral registration in accordance with the prescribed
legal procedure. Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh today launched the revamped
websites of Ministry of Defence and Department of Defence. The Defence
Ministry said that the modern, accessible and user-friendly platforms are
fully compliant with the digital brand identity manual 3.0 and the guidelines
for Indian government websites 3.0. A Houthi missile attack on a military
training centre in Yemen's Shabwa government has killed more than 53
three recruits and injured over 200 others, according to preliminary figures, released
by Shabwa Governorate Media Office.
In a statement issued today, the local authority said the recruits were undergoing training
and security qualification at the Mata Ahmad al-Suleimani Training Centre when it came
under bombardment by several ballistic missiles.
The authority condemned the attack, holding the Houthi militias responsible.
The police prefecture of Bouche-du-Ronde in southern France today banned all gatherings
and demonstrations throughout the city of Marseille from noon to 8pm local time.
French President Emmanuel Macron has vowed legal action against those responsible for
violence during protests across the country on Saturday.
In France, nationwide demonstrations on Saturday drew some 5,50,000 participants, uniting
farmers, trade unions, climate activists and students demanding relief from high-fueled
prices, inflation and public service cuts.
The gatherings rapidly descended into violent clashes.
According to the French Interior Ministry, 997 police officers and gendarmes were injured,
seven of them seriously, while 2,397 people were arrested nationwide.
Protests against the rising cost of living also swept northern Italy, Belgium's capital
Brussels, Lisbon, Porto, Quimbra and other Portuguese cities.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has reached Tushanbe in Tajikistan this evening on a two-day official
visit to represent India at the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government of
the Shanghai Cooperation Organization. The meeting is scheduled to be held tomorrow.
The Indian Embassy in Italy has issued an advisory for Indian nationals in view of
the protests and demonstrations held in some Italian cities last week. In a social
media posts, the embassy has advised Indian nationals to exercise caution, avoid crowded
areas and locations where protests are taking place and follow local news about such events.
It has also requested Indian nationals to contact on phone number
plus 39-331-614-2085 and plus 39-388-1647527 in case of an emergency.
At the Asian Paragames in Japan, India bagged 11 medals including four gold, five silver
and two bronze on day one at Aichi Nagoya today. Nishad Kumar clinched India's first
para-athletics gold, winning the men's long-jump in T-47 category. In women's 1500m T-12
T-13 event, Somya won gold while Radha Venkatesh secured silver. Ravanni, Valsaneni won
bronze in women's 1500-meter T-11 event. In the men's javelin F-46 event, Rinku clenched
gold and Ajit Singh won silver. Early today, in the women's 10-meter air rifle SH-1 event,
Mona Garwal claimed the gold with a game's record, but Avni Lekhara took the silver
as India opened its medal account with the top two finish. Visually impaired, Jhudoka
Kokila won silver medal in women's J-252 KG category, while Kapil Parmar won bronze
in men's J170KG category. In swimming, Ravi Kartik won silver in men's 100m freestyle
S13 event. India's medal tally has risen to 11, including four gold, five silver and two
bronze medals. President Draupadi Murmur and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have congratulated
the medal winners.
The festival of Navratri has reached its final day across Gujarat and Mahanavmi is being
celebrated with great religious fervour. We have a report.
The nine-day grand festival of Sardai Navratri comes to a peaceful and devotional close today
across the state of Gujarat.
For the past nine days, households and public venues lead sacred lamps to honor the various
manifestations of Goddess Durga.
Today, garbha grounds, streets and residential compounds across every city are geared up
for the ultimate night of music and dance.
Tomorrow, on the auspicious occasion of Dasera, special events will take place
across residential societies to offer final prayers and seek divine blazings.
On the occasion, people will respectfully submerge the sacred garbis, jawaras and colors into
nearby rivers and lakes, marking the formal end of the vibrant cultural celebration with
Aparna Kut, Arsalpandya Akaswani News, Ahmedabad.
In West Bengal, the Mahashtami of Durga Puja festival is being celebrated with traditional
fervour across the state.
Today is Mahashtami.
People are gathering before the puja pandals across the state for the blessings of Madurga.
Strict vajals are in place for the effective crowd control in the puja pandals.
Earlier in the day, Mahasthami puja, Anjali, Shondhi puja and other rituals have been performed
before the idol of Madurga in all the puja pandals and family pujas in Bengal.
Kumari puja which is a special ritual of Belur mod and other Hindu mod have also
been performed.
In our bilingual live phone and program public speak tonight at 9.30, we will bring an insightful
discussion on consumer awareness and protection with Anupam Mishra, Additional Secretary, Ministry
of Consumer Affairs and Dr. Sheetal Kapoor, expert on consumer affairs.
And now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Free trade agreement with New Zealand to come into force on the occasion of Vijay
After Dasmi tomorrow, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal says FTA will open new
opportunities for countries' exporters.
Government asks Meta not to expose users to disproportionate or one-sided narratives on
its platforms.
Action to be taken against online platforms or unauthorized sale of regulated explosive
substances.
New Delhi rejects anti-India references and organization of Islamic cooperation resolutions
accuses Pakistan of misusing the organization.
Utti attack on Yemen army camp in Shabwa kills 53 soldiers.
And in Asian Barra games, India bags 11 medals including four gold and five silver to take
it's standing to fourth position on day one.
That is all in the news at 9.
Good night.
